definitions.explanation: A widespread infectious disease that affects many people in a region at the same time. Used broadly for both historical plagues and modern epidemics, often with a somewhat literary or formal tone.

examples.japanese: {疫病|えきびょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{広|ひろ}がった→広がる：01980_hirogaru⟧。
⟦{中世|ちゅうせい}→中世：05524_chuusei⟧⟦ヨーロッパ→ヨーロッパ：00427_yooroppa⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{疫病|えきびょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{亡|な}くなった→亡くなる：02639_nakunaru⟧。
examples.english: In medieval Europe, many people died from epidemics.

examples.japanese: {疫病|えきびょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{流行|りゅうこう}→流行：03678_ryuukou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{防|ふせ}ぐ→防ぐ：02409_fusegu⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{政府|せいふ}→政府：03294_seifu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}った→取る：00565_toru⟧。
examples.english: In order to prevent the spread of the epidemic, the government took strict measures.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat formal or literary word for epidemic or plague. In modern Japanese, ⟦{感染症|かんせんしょう}→感染症：15681_kansenshou⟧ (infectious disease) and ⟦{伝染病|でんせんびょう}→伝染病：29731_densenbyou⟧ (contagious disease) are more common in everyday and medical contexts, while {疫病|えきびょう} tends to appear in historical narratives and dramatic descriptions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疫病|えきびょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{流行|りゅうこう}→流行：03678_ryuukou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: an epidemic breaks out
- {疫病|えきびょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{蔓延|まんえん}→蔓延：09460_manen⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: an epidemic spreads widely
- {疫病|えきびょう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{罹|かか}る: to contract an epidemic disease
- {疫病神|やくびょうがみ}: god of pestilence; jinx, person who brings bad luck
